Using the nucleon coalescence model based on the kinetic freeze-out nucleons from the hybrid model of MUSIC hydrodynamics and UrQMD hadronic transport model, the PI and 3 his collaborator have studied anti-deuteron production and its event-by-event fluctuation in √ Pb+Pb collisions at s = 5.02 TeV [11]. A clear suppression of the anti-deuteron to NN antiproton yield ratio was found in peripheral collisions as in the measurements from the ALICE Collaboration. For those theoretical events that fit the measured net-proton number fluctuation, the model can also describe the net-proton number fluctuation and the negative correlation between the antiproton and anti-deuteron multiplicities at large pseudorapidity acceptance as observed in ALICE experiments. Using the coalescence model with the phase-space information of proton and neutron pairs from a multiphase transport (AMPT) model at the kinetic freezeout, the PI and his √ collaborators have studied jet-associated deuteron production in pp collisions at s = 13 √ TeV and p-Pb collisions at s = 5.02 TeV [12]. Although the in-jet coalescence factor for NN deuterons of low transverse momentum, given by the ratio of the in-jet deuteron number to the square of the in-jet proton number, is found to be larger than the coalescence factor in the medium perpendicular to the jet direction by a factor of about 10 in pp collisions and 25 in p-Pb collisions as observed in the ALICE measurements at the LHC, such enhancements mainly come from coalescence of nucleons inside the jet with nucleons in the medium. Only at higher transverse momentum can deuteron production from the coalescence of nucleons inside the jet dominate over that from the medium nucleons, providing a new window to probe the phase-space structure of nucleons inside jets.
